visual_text: Which alarm wakes someone with hearing loss?
Out of 100 adults with mild to moderately severe hearing loss in deep sleep, in a laboratory.
Vibrating pad under pillow or mattress: 80 to 84
38 adults aged 18 to 80; deep sleep only; not only older people
Sleep without hearing aids? Check your alarm
Illustration. Visits are offered by every fire and rescue service in England; what they fit varies.
1  Hearing aids out at night: ask for an alarm you will wake to
2  Ask for a vibrating pad, not only a flashing light
3  Ask your fire and rescue service for a home fire safety visit and say you are hard of hearing
Bruck and Thomas, Ear Hear 2009; James and Clark 2025
Alasdair MacLullich | Small detail, real effect
alt_text: Bar chart of how many out of 100 adults with hearing loss were woken from deep sleep in a laboratory: standard high-pitched alarm 56, lower-pitched alarm 92, vibrating pad 80 to 84, flashing light 27. 38 adults aged 18 to 80.

Illustration of an older Black woman asleep in bed, a hearing aid, glass and phone on the bedside table, a vibrating pad under the pillow and a smoke alarm on the ceiling. Three numbered tips: alarm you will wake to, vibrating pad, and a fire and rescue home safety visit.
